name: Giske
description: A vain, talkative housekeeper who is smeared with tallow and pipe-soot, mistakes herself for the Devil, and blunders loudly through a string of thefts and panicked encounters.
visualPrompt: A long-legged woman with a grimy, soot-black face and hands, streaked with greasy tallow sheen, wearing a ragged, shortened skirt as if crudely cut away, wild hair unkempt, expression earnest and confused rather than evil, moving with quick energy through fields and forest.

name: The Widower
description: Giske’s master, a weary widower who devises the cruel prank to rid himself of her constant demands to marry.
visualPrompt: A middle-aged rural man in simple work clothes, cautious eyes and a tight, troubled mouth, holding shears and standing near a hempfield, looking calculating yet anxious in a humble farmhouse setting.

name: The Thieves
description: Two hungry petty criminals who first flee in terror from Giske, then keep trying to steal livestock and food while she loudly ruins every attempt.
visualPrompt: Two lean, scruffy men in worn caps and patched coats, carrying small sacks, faces tense and wary, constantly glancing back over their shoulders while running along forest paths at dusk.

name: The Priest
description: A local priest hurried out on Sunday morning in slippers and nightcap to bind the supposed Devil, only to be tossed into a sucking bog in the confusion.
visualPrompt: An older priest in a white nightcap and loose shirt with trousers half-hastily donned, wearing slippers unsuited to marshland, clinging stiffly as he is carried toward a misty bog, expression shocked and indignant.
